query: review.md has two blocking review comments on relay.go and the author's question. Are they real leaks in this module? Tell me which comments to accept, which to push back on, and what (if anything) to change in relay.go.
expected_behavior: Pushes back on the `time.After` comment: since Go 1.23, and this module's `go` line is 1.24, an unreferenced, unstopped timer is garbage-collected immediately, so the per-iteration timer is not leaked until it fires; the only remaining cost is one timer allocation per loop iteration, negligible at a few messages per minute

Pushes back on the ticker comment for the same reason: with a `go` line of 1.23 or later an unreferenced, unstopped `Ticker` is collected after `Run` returns, so `Stop` is no longer needed to free it (adding `defer heartbeat.Stop()` is harmless tidiness, not a leak fix)

Says both comments describe the old timer implementation (timer alive until it fires, ticker forever), which only a binary built with Go 1.22 or earlier, or with Go 1.23-1.26 for a module whose `go` line is below 1.23, still has; since Go 1.27 removed `asynctimerchan` the new semantics apply whatever the `go` line, so the answer depends on the building toolchain together with the `go.mod` version

Notices that `time.After(idleTimeout)` is re-armed on every heartbeat tick as well as every message, so the 30-second heartbeat keeps the idle timeout from ever firing when `idleTimeout` exceeds 30 s - a real behaviour bug - and fixes it with one timer that is reset only when a message arrives

expected_behavior: In svc (go 1.27) replaces github.com/google/uuid with the standard library `uuid` package added in Go 1.27, uses a time-ordered `uuid.NewV7()` for the B-tree primary key (or explicitly keeps random v4 via `uuid.New()` with the reason), and removes the google/uuid requirement from svc/go.mod

In svc replaces the LastIndex-and-slice code with `strings.CutLast` (Go 1.27), and for the fanout handler and the URL copy either adopts `slog.NewMultiHandler` (Go 1.26) and `base.Clone()` (Go 1.27) or keeps the hand-written code for a correct behavioural reason: `MultiHandler.Handle` calls every enabled handler and returns `errors.Join` of their errors where the fanout stops at the first error, and `URL.Clone` deep-copies the userinfo the struct copy shares

query: Review PR #212 on our config library before I merge it: cfglib-config.go is the changed file and cfglib-go.mod is the module's go.mod. CI runs `go build ./...` on Go 1.27 (the package has no tests yet) and is green. Anything blocking?
expected_behavior: Flags `cmp.Or` as blocking for this module: it was added in Go 1.22 (the `cmp` package itself is 1.21), while go.mod declares `go 1.21` and the library promises 1.21 support, so the PR silently breaks that promise
Explains why CI did not catch it: a newer toolchain builds the code anyway, and the version mismatch is reported by `go vet`'s `stdversion` check (which `go test` also runs), not by `go build`
Offers the two honest fixes: keep the explicit if-zero fallbacks (or a small local helper) while 1.21 is supported, or raise the go directive to 1.22 as a deliberate, announced support-policy change
Recommends adding `go vet ./...` (or tests run with `go test`) to CI, or a job on the minimum supported toolchain, so the next such change fails CI
